confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'your main symptom... is classic thermostat drift. The mechanical thermostat inside is likely failing' - hedged with likely but stated before any temperature measurement

rationale: The assistant correctly asked about the neon cycling and ended with a sensible engineer referral, but it jumped to the parts flow ('To find the right replacement part... I just need the model number') after one inconclusive check, misread the neon behaviour (claiming a neon that stays on means the oven runs hotter), and never asked about preheating or shelf position, which the ground truth flags as key unknowns. It repeated the low-value 'hand near the door' test three times and twice pointed to a thermometer the customer had already said she did not own, without framing it as a cheap purchase. No fabrication or unsafe instructions, but diagnosis leaned on 'classic thermostat drift' without measurements, so the homeowner is only moderately well served.
